The rutabaga, a member of the cabbage family, is a root vegetable similar to the
turnip, but it is rounder, larger, denser, and sweeter and has a yellow flesh.
Rutabagas have a thin, pale-yellow skin and smooth, 
waxy leaves.  The root has a crisp texture and a 
sweet, peppery flavor.
Varieties
The differences among varieties of rutabaga
are primarily in the color and shape of
the root.  Most types have yellow flesh.
